column1: # A row is an attestation with a justification: bytes is the sum of the frames along
# the path its evidence names (reserve-harness/paths/<board>/<item>.tsv), traced by
# hand from the source at commit dccb0959 and recomputed from a fresh
# CONFIG_STACK_USAGE=y build by tests/app/reserves.sh where the path has .su steps;
# a path of hardware-frame and assembly literals only (thread_switch, pendsv, svc,
# guard_area) is read from the source and not recomputed. It is never an observed
# high-water mark: the harness's marks only try to refute it. applies_when names the
# board and the Kconfig symbols whose setting would add or remove a call or a push on
# that path, read from each function's source (=n: not set); a build with no
# applicable row for a needed item has verdict unknown, never a default.
# The isr_<driver> items are one per driver interrupt handler in the board's
# inventory: Zephyr's common entry and exit (isr_entry_exit) plus the handler's own
# frames; the system timer's is timer_dispatch; svc is the SVC exception's. The
# drv_<member> items are Zephyr's part of a board member's call (the driver operation
# under the inline API), added to the adapter's measured frames in its provider evidence.
# drv_adc_read is the Adc sampler thread's blocking read path (the driver's read to its
# wait for completion), a term of that thread's requirement with thread_kernel_calls.
# frdm_imxrt1186_cm7 (decision 0023, the board's Cortex-M7) takes frdm_imxrt1186's paths: recomputed over
# the harness built for frdm_imxrt1186/mimxrt1186/cm7 under both fragments, each sums to the M33's bytes. Its
# console transport is interrupt-driven (boards/frdm_imxrt1186_cm7.conf), so it has uart_calls for that
# configuration and isr_lpuart, recomputed over the harness built with the board's conf and overlays.
